# Adjudication Task — Chapter 569

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃569화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|쿵.
  6|
  7|등 뒤에서 문이 닫히는 소리가 천둥처럼 울려 퍼졌다. 동시에 일흔이라는 나이가 무색할 만큼 건장한 체구를 지닌 그, 송천우의 신형이 비틀거렸다.
  8|
  9|스륵, 탁.
 10|
 11|강대한 마나도, 지금까지 산전수전을 겪으며 쌓아 올린 경륜도 지금만큼은 무소용이다.
 12|
 13|벽면을 붙잡고 바닥만 빤히 노려보는 그의 시야에, 한 쌍의 검은 구두가 불쑥 비집고 들어왔다.
 14|
 15|“괜찮으십니까?”
 16|
 17|귓가를 파고드는 사무적인 목소리. 고개를 들어 구두의 주인을 확인한 송천우가 이를 악물었다.
 18|
 19|“지금 이게…… 괜찮아 보이느냐?”
 20|
 21|불꽃이 튀는 그의 눈동자에, 경호팀장 고세원이 고개를 숙였다.
 22|
 23|“불편하게 들리셨다면 죄송합니다.”
 24|
 25|“마음에도 없는 소리는 집어치워라. 당장 네놈의 목을 꺾어 버리기 전에!”
 26|
 27|“그다지 권하고 싶은 방법은 아니군요. 득은 없고, 실만 있을 겁니다.”
 28|
 29|고세원은 말과 함께 손을 부드럽게 내저었다.
 30|
 31|심상치 않은 기색을 눈치채고 저 멀리 복도 끝에서 막 걸음을 떼려던 경호팀원들이 움직임을 멈췄다.
 32|
 33|“제 밑에 있는 친구들인데, 지사장님께서도 아시다시피 실력이 꽤 좋습니다. 상황이 닥치면 물불 안 가리는 면모도 있고요.”
 34|
 35|“네놈…….”
 36|
 37|“오해 없으시길 바랍니다. 더 이상 상황을 악화시키지 않으셨으면 하는 마음에 드리는 말씀입니다.”
 38|
 39|콰득.
 40|
 41|벽을 짚은 손아귀에 힘이 실리자 강화 마법이 걸린 대리석 벽면이 거미줄처럼 갈라졌다.
 42|
 43|핏발 선 눈으로 고세원을 노려보던 송천우가 씹어 뱉듯이 입을 열었다.
 44|
 45|“그래서 이 일과는 아무런 상관도, 죄도 없는 우리 애들을 납치했나?”
 46|
 47|“그런 것치고는 방비가 철두철미하더군요. 지사장님께서도 일말의 가능성 정도는 염두에 두셨다는 뜻이겠죠.”
 48|
 49|경호팀 전원이 습격했음에도 두 명의 사망자가 발생했다.
 50|
 51|아레스 길드 내에서도 최정예로 꼽히는 그들의 수준을 생각한다면, 두 명의 사망자 앞에는 ‘무려’라는 두 글자가 붙어야 한다.
 52|
 53|“가족분들의 일에 관해서는 저도 유감스럽게 생각합니다만. 사전에 의심하셨다면 그 이상의 전력을 투입해서라도 지켰어야 했습니다.”
 54|
 55|“……!”
 56|
 57|“괜한 말을 했군요. 죄송합니다.”
 58|
 59|고세원의 말은 진심이었다. 송천우는 이미 죽을 날을 받아 둔 늙은 사자나 다름없는 상황. 굳이 자신이 나서서 가슴에 비수를 꽃을 필요까지는 없었다.
 60|
 61|‘안타까움에 튀어나온 말이라고 하면, 이자는 믿을까.’
 62|
 63|그도 가장이다. 마흔이 넘어 처음으로 본 아들도, 몇 달 후 태어날 둘째는 벌써부터 눈에 넣어도 아프지 않았다.
 64|
 65|고세원은 자식들의 안전과 행복을 위해서라면 목숨도 바칠 수 있었다. 그것이 아버지고, 부모였으니까.
 66|
 67|하지만 송천우는 자신의 야심과 가족들의 안위를 저울추에 올려놨다.
 68|
 69|하긴, 최악의 상황을 생각했다면 석고준을 적으로 돌릴 시도조차 안 했을 것이다.
 70|
 71|‘……내가 할 수 있는 말은 아니지만.’
 72|
 73|고세원은 스스로가 병신 같은 악당처럼 느껴졌다.
 74|
 75|근 십수 년 동안 헌터보다는 해결사라 부를 만한 인생을 살아온 그다.
 76|
 77|이정룡의 눈에 들어 경호팀에 들어온 이후 주 표적은 몬스터가 아닌 사람이었으니까.
 78|
 79|팀원들에게 송천우의 가족들을 납치하라는 명령을 내리고 깔끔하게 뒤처리를 한 것도 그였다.
 80|
 81|‘그런 주제에 누구에게 훈계질을.’
 82|
 83|결국 모두가 같은 똥통 속의 똥일 뿐이다.
 84|
 85|송천우는 은퇴를 앞두고 야심에 불타올라 위험을 자초했고, 석고준은 수단과 방법을 가리지 않고 칼을 휘둘렀으며, 고세원은 상관이 휘두르는 검이 되어 송천우의 가족을 납치했다.
 86|
 87|‘나쁜 놈들 간의 전쟁. 끝에 남은 건 승자와 패자뿐이지.’
 88|
 89|그리고 자신은 부속품에 불과하다.
 90|
 91|고세원이 씁쓸하게 입맛을 다시던 그때.
 92|
 93|와락!
 94|
 95|칠순 노인의 것이라곤 생각하기 힘든 단단한 손아귀가 그의 멱살을 붙들었다.
 96|
 97|“팀장님!”
 98|
 99|“됐다. 자리나 지켜.”
100|
101|팀원들을 만류한 고세원이 머리 하나는 큰 송천우를 덤덤하게 응시했다.
102|
103|“이미 말씀드렸습니다. 득보다 실이 많을 거라고.”
104|
105|“네놈, 네놈들이 감히 내 새끼들을……!”
106|
107|“부 길드장님께서 안에서 듣고 계실 겁니다. 두 분이서 무슨 대화를 나누셨는지는 모르겠습니다만, 그래도 추가적인 희생은 없었으면 합니다.”
108|
109|“……!”
110|
111|가족들의 명줄을 틀어쥔 석고준의 심기를 거스르지 말라는 뜻.
112|
113|그 말에 담긴 의미를 즉각 알아차린 송천우의 눈꺼풀이 잘게 떨렸다.
114|
115|이를 악문 채 고세원을 노려보던 그의 손아귀에서 스르륵 힘이 풀렸다.
116|
117|“잘 생각하셨습니다.”
118|
119|“……주둥이 닥쳐라. 마음 같아서는 당장 네놈의 면상을 뭉개 버리고 싶으니까.”
120|
121|“그러시겠죠.”
122|
123|고세원의 입가에 씁쓸한 미소가 스쳤다. 자신 같았어도 그와 같은 반응을 보였을 테니까.
124|
125|그리고 냉정하게 평가했을 때, 송천우는 현역에서 물러난 지 이십 년이 지난 지금에도 충분히 대단한 실력자였다.
126|
127|지닌바 능력이 야심에 비해 모자랐을 뿐. 한때나마 이정룡의 정적(政敵)이었다는 것만으로도 그를 설명하기에는 충분하다.
128|
129|‘그래서 굳이 이런 지저분한 방법을 택한 거고.’
130|
131|이번에 석고준이 택한 방식은 마음에 들지 않지만, 지저분한 만큼 효과는 확실하다.
132|
133|빠른 시일 내에 송천우는 제거될 것이다. 누구도 의심을 품지 못할 만큼 아주 자연스럽게.
134|
135|“따라오십시오. 밖까지 안내해 드리겠습니다.”
136|
137|목례를 취한 고세원이 먼저 걸음을 옮기자, 고개를 돌려 굳게 닫힌 문을 한차례 노려본 송천우가 뒤를 따랐다.
138|
139|저벅. 저벅.
140|
141|고세원이 팀원들을 물린 탓에 복도에는 두 사람의 걸음 소리만 울려 퍼졌다.
142|
143|그리고 짧게 이어지는 적막함을 깨트린 것은 송천우의 한마디였다.
144|
145|“아까 했던 말. 사실이냐?”
146|
147|“……?”
148|
149|“석고준과 내가 무슨 대화를 나눴는지 모르겠다고 한 것, 사실이냐고 물었다.”
150|
151|잠시 말에 담긴 뜻을 생각하던 고세원이 묵묵히 고개를 끄덕였다.
152|
153|“그렇군. 하긴, 조사해 본 바로는 네놈도 책사와는 거리가 멀지.”
154|
155|“그게 무슨.”
156|
157|“생각했던 것만큼 신임받는 수하는 아닌 모양이군. 아니면 최측근에게도 숨기고 싶던가.”
158|
159|미간을 찌푸린 고세원의 모습에, 송천우가 힘없는 실소를 흘렸다.
160|
161|“이봐, 고세원이.”
162|
163|잠깐 사이 십 년. 아니 이십 년은 늙어 버린 그가 허탈한 목소리로 말을 이었다.
164|
165|“사람에게는 무릇 정도라는 게 있는 법이야. 알고 있나?”
166|
167|“……부길드장님을 비난하시는 거라면. 그쯤에서 멈추라고 말씀드리고 싶군요.”
168|
169|“비난이라, 생각했던 것 이상으로 부드러운 단어군. 석고준 그놈에게 쓰기에는 턱없이 부족해.”
170|
171|“심정은 이해합니다. 하지만 이 일에 관련된 그 누구도 서로를 욕할 수 없습니다. 저 역시 지사장님께서도 그리 깨끗하게 살아오지 않으셨다는 것 정도는 알고 있고요.”
172|
173|“허허, 그렇지. 한때는 나 역시 목적을 위해 수단과 방법을 가리지 않았던 적이 있었지. 하지만 이 정도까지는 아니었어.”
174|
175|실성한 듯 공허한 웃음을 터트리는 송천우의 모습에, 고세원은 문득 입을 다물었다.
176|
177|지금 그가 말하고자 하는 것이 비단 납치에 관한 것만이 아니라는 것을 깨달은 것이다.
178|
179|‘뭐지?’
180|
181|쿵쿵. 가슴이 뛰고 전류가 등골을 훑고 지나간다.
182|
183|이건 경고다. 들어서는 안 된다는 위험 신호. 하지만 그의 몸은 생각과 반대로 움직이고 있었다.
184|
185|“뭡니까. 지사장님께서 말씀하시는 그 정도라는 것이.”
186|
187|“최소한의 본분도 잊어버린, 괴물.”
188|
189|“네?”
190|
191|저벅.
192|
193|송천우의 발걸음이 우뚝 멈췄다. 밖으로 향하는 텔레포트 마법진을 말없이 바라보던 그가 말을 이었다.
194|
195|“인간과 괴물의 경계. 석고준 그놈은…… 이미 괴물이 되어 버렸어.”
196|
197|문득 노인의 텅 빈 눈빛이 허공을 훑었다.
198|
199|찬란했던 과거의 기억을 더듬던 송천우는 마법진을 향해 힘없이 걸음을 내디뎠다.
200|
201|간절함이 담긴 한 마디를 남긴 채.
202|
203|“내가 자네에게 했던 행동에 대해서는 사과하겠네. 그러니 부디, 그 아이들이 덧없이 죽는 것만큼은 막아 주게.”
204|
205|그것이 마지막이었다.
206|
207|파앗!
208|
209|고세원이 뭐라 되물을 새도 없이, 텔레포트 마법이 발현되며 눈부신 광채가 한 사람의 신형을 집어삼켰다.
210|
211|홀로 남은 채 혼란스러운 눈빛으로 송천우가 서 있던 자리를 바라보던 고세원은 문득 고개를 돌렸다.
212|
213|온통 새하얀 대리석으로 이루어진 복도.
214|
215|그리고 끝없이 이어진 복도 끝에 굳게 닫힌 문과, 그 안에서 흡족한 기분으로 와인을 홀짝이고 있을 누군가.
216|
217|‘도대체…… 무슨 일을 벌이신 겁니까.’
218|
219|고세원은 마음 깊은 곳 어딘가를 향해 중얼거렸다.
220|
221|언제나 환했던 A구역이, 오늘만큼은 어둠이 가득한 구렁텅이처럼 느껴졌다.
222|
223|
224|
225|* * *
226|
227|
228|
229|연무장. 현대에서는 트레이닝 룸이라고 부르는 이곳에 얼마나 틀어박혀 있었는지 모르겠다.
230|
231|하루. 이틀. 어쩌면 사흘.
232|
233|사방이 가로막혀 있고 온도가 조절되는 이곳에서 무공에 몰두하다 보니 시간의 흐름을 제대로 느낄 수 없었다.
234|
235|스마트폰이 있어도 들여다보지 않으니 알 수 없었고, 그런 내 사정을 어렴풋이 알았는지, 평화 길드의 누구도 나를 찾아오거나 연락하지 않았다.
236|
237|“…….”
238|
239|말하다 보니까 아싸가 따로 없지만. 그건 절대 아니다.
240|
241|……아마도 아닐 거다.
242|
243|‘스켈레톤 킹. 그 녀석도 그 후로는 한 번도 안 찾아왔고.’
244|
245|녀석이 생각보다 잘 해결해 내고 있다는 증거이니 희소식이긴 한데, 그만큼 긴급 구조팀이 바빠졌으며 이상 현상을 보이는 게이트가 많아졌다는 뜻이니 마냥 기뻐할 수는 없는 일이다.
246|
247|그리고 그런 의미에서, 내가 시도하는 일이 거의 마무리 되어 가고 있다는 건 분명 확실한 희소식이 맞았다.
248|
249|‘물론 아직까지는 미완성이지만.’
250|
251|처음 시도해 보는 것이라 그런지, 지금까지의 과정은 결코 쉽지 않았다.
252|
253|어쩌면 일촉즉발과도 같은 현재 상황에 맞물려 그만큼 뛰어난 것을 만들어야 한다는 부담감도 한몫했을 것이다.
254|
255|‘지금까지만 해도 충분히 괜찮을 것 같기는 한데…….’
256|
257|그냥 이대로 확 질러 버릴까.
258|
259|지금까지 수십, 수백 번이나 떠올렸던 그 고민을 다시 머릿속에서 반복하던 그때.
260|
261|익숙한 기계음과 함께 굳게 닫혀 있던 트레이닝 룸의 출입문이 열렸다.
262|
263|“여기 있었군. 마침 자네의 도움이 필요해.”
264|

## Adjudicator rules

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)
* a rebuilt joke whose comic machine BASE already has (`얼마나 …는지 …겠다` must stay a simple exaggeration: “snored so loudly even my mother in Ilsan probably heard him,” not “You had to wonder how loudly…”)
* dropped image, attitude, or timing
* SOL replaces an established project rendering, System label, or Markdown convention with an unsupported synonym
* SOL stamps `hyung` (or another kinship title) onto every narrative name when BASE already uses the name and the Korean `형` is ordinary reference, not a vocative or a topical joke (`진호 형` → Jinho in narration)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

## `REPAIR` only when both fail

Example: `겹경사가 따로 없다` means two good things **together** (double blessing). `따로` is not “separate.” If BASE says “entirely separate stroke of luck” and SOL says “unexpected windfall,” `REPAIR` to stacked luck.

Do not `REPAIR` a working SOL line. Do not invent a third style because you prefer it.

For `REPAIR`, write the smallest complete replacement needed for that hunk. It must be natural English and fully source-faithful.

Korean **keys** are binding unless the source uses that string in a different ordinary-language sense. Glossary **English** is not a license for a calque (`presiding chair`). If SOL is a natural recast of the same sense, keep SOL.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.

## Adjudicator rules

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)
* a rebuilt joke whose comic machine BASE already has (`얼마나 …는지 …겠다` must stay a simple exaggeration: “snored so loudly even my mother in Ilsan probably heard him,” not “You had to wonder how loudly…”)
* dropped image, attitude, or timing
* SOL replaces an established project rendering, System label, or Markdown convention with an unsupported synonym
* SOL stamps `hyung` (or another kinship title) onto every narrative name when BASE already uses the name and the Korean `형` is ordinary reference, not a vocative or a topical joke (`진호 형` → Jinho in narration)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

## `REPAIR` only when both fail

Example: `겹경사가 따로 없다` means two good things **together** (double blessing). `따로` is not “separate.” If BASE says “entirely separate stroke of luck” and SOL says “unexpected windfall,” `REPAIR` to stacked luck.

Do not `REPAIR` a working SOL line. Do not invent a third style because you prefer it.

For `REPAIR`, write the smallest complete replacement needed for that hunk. It must be natural English and fully source-faithful.

## Glossary

Korean **keys** are binding unless the source uses that string in a different ordinary-language sense. Glossary **English** is not a license for a calque (`presiding chair`). If SOL is a natural recast of the same sense, keep SOL.

Reasons must name the veto, or say that SOL keeps sense and voice. Do not merely say one version is "better" or "more natural" without stating what changed.

Keep reasons brief. Do not adjudicate unchanged passages. Do not call tools.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.

At the sound of the businesslike voice, Song looked up, saw who the shoes belonged to, and gritted his teeth.

[P9]
“Do I look all right to you?”

[P10]
Head of Security Go Se-won bowed beneath his furious glare.

[P11]
“I’m sorry if that sounded insensitive.”

[P12]
“Spare me the words you don’t mean. Before I break your neck!”

[P13]
“I wouldn’t recommend it. You’d have nothing to gain and plenty to lose.”

[P14]
Go Se-won gave a gentle wave of his hand. At the far end of the hallway, the security-team members who had started toward them stopped.

[P15]
“They’re my men. As you know, Director, they’re quite capable. And when the situation calls for it, they won’t hesitate.”

[P16]
“You…”

[P17]
“Please don’t misunderstand me. I only mean that I don’t want you to make matters worse.”

[P18]
*Crack.*

[P19]
The marble beneath Song’s hand, reinforced by magic, split in a spiderweb of cracks. He glared at Go Se-won through bloodshot eyes and forced the words through his teeth.

[P20]
“So you kidnapped my children? They had nothing to do with this. They’d done nothing wrong.”

[P21]
“They were exceptionally well guarded for people who had nothing to do with it. You must have considered the possibility, Director.”

[P22]
Two security-team members had died despite the whole team taking part in the attack. Given that they were among the best Ares Guild had to offer, it was *no fewer than* two.

[P23]
“I regret what happened to your family. But if you suspected this might happen, you should have sent even more people to protect them.”

[P24]
“……!”

[P25]
“I shouldn’t have said that. I apologize.”

[P26]
Go Se-won meant it. Song Cheonwoo was already like an old lion whose death had been decided. There was no need for Go Se-won to drive the knife in himself.

[P27]
*Would he believe me if I said it slipped out because I felt sorry for him?*

[P28]
Go Se-won was a father too. His first son had been born after he turned forty, and his second child was due in a few months. Both were already more precious to him than anything.

[P29]
He would give his life for his children’s safety and happiness. That was what it meant to be a father. A parent.

[P30]
But Song Cheonwoo had weighed his ambition against his family’s safety. Then again, if he had imagined the worst, he would never have tried to make an enemy of Go Jun.

[P31]
*……Not that I’m one to talk.*

[P32]
Go Se-won felt like a pathetic villain.

[P33]
For well over a decade, he had lived more like a fixer than a Hunter. Ever since Lee Jungryong had noticed him and brought him into the security team, his main targets had been people, not monsters.

[P34]
He had ordered his men to kidnap Song Cheonwoo’s family. He had made sure they covered their tracks.

[P35]
*And I have the nerve to lecture him.*

[P36]
They were all pieces of shit in the same shit pit.

[P37]
Song Cheonwoo had let ambition consume him on the verge of retirement and brought danger upon himself. Go Jun swung his blade without caring what it took to get his way. And Go Se-won had become the sword in his superior’s hand and kidnapped Song’s family.

[P38]
*A war between bastards. In the end, there’ll be a winner and a loser.*

[P39]
Go Se-won was nothing more than a part of it.

[P40]
He was swallowing the bitter thought when—

[P41]
*Grab!*

[P42]
A hand far too strong to belong to a seventy-year-old man seized his collar.

[P43]
“Team Leader!”

[P44]
“Enough. Stay at your posts.”

[P45]
Go Se-won stopped his men and calmly looked up at Song Cheonwoo, who stood a full head taller than him.

[P46]
“I told you. You stand to lose more than you’d gain.”

[P47]
“You bastards dare lay a hand on my children…!”

[P48]
“The Vice Guild Master can hear us from inside. I don’t know what the two of you discussed, but I don’t want there to be any more casualties.”

[P49]
“……!”

[P50]
Go Jun held his family’s lives in his hands. Go Se-won was telling him not to make Go Jun angry.

[P51]
Song understood at once. His eyelids trembled, and though he kept glaring at Go Se-won through clenched teeth, his grip slowly loosened.

[P52]
“You made the right choice.”

[P53]
“……Shut your mouth. I’d like nothing more than to smash your face in right now.”

[P54]
“I’m sure you would.”

[P55]
A bitter smile touched Go Se-won’s lips. He would have felt the same in Song’s place.

[P56]
And even twenty years after leaving active service, Song Cheonwoo was still an extraordinary fighter. His ability simply hadn’t matched his ambition. The fact that he had once been Lee Jungryong’s political rival said enough about him.

[P57]
*Which is why Go Jun chose a method this dirty.*

[P58]
Go Se-won disliked it. But dirty as it was, it would work.

[P59]
Song Cheonwoo would be eliminated soon, and it would look so natural that no one would suspect a thing.

[P60]
“Follow me. I’ll escort you outside.”

[P61]
Go Se-won bowed slightly and started down the hallway. Song cast one last glare at the closed door, then followed.

[P62]
*Step. Step.*

[P63]
Go Se-won had sent his men away. Only their footsteps sounded in the hallway until Song broke the silence.

[P64]
“What you said earlier. Was it true?”

[P65]
“……?”

[P66]
“That you don’t know what Go Jun and I discussed. Was that true?”

[P67]
Go Se-won considered the question for a moment, then nodded.

[P68]
“I see. From what I found out about you, I suppose you were never much of a strategist.”

[P69]
“What do you mean?”

[P70]
“It seems he doesn’t trust you as much as I thought. Or perhaps he wanted to hide it even from his closest aide.”

[P71]
Song gave a weak, hollow laugh at Go Se-won’s frown.

[P72]
“Go Se-won.”

[P73]
In those few moments, he seemed to have aged ten years. No, twenty. His voice was drained of strength.

[P74]
“There are limits to what a person should do. Do you understand?”

[P75]
“……If you’re criticizing the Vice Guild Master, I’d ask you to stop.”

[P76]
“Criticizing him? That’s a much gentler word than I’d expected. Far too gentle for that bastard Go Jun.”

[P77]
“I understand how you feel. But no one involved in this has the right to condemn anyone else. I know you haven’t lived a particularly clean life either, Director.”

[P78]
“Heh. True. There was a time when I’d use any means necessary to get what I wanted. But I never went this far.”

[P79]
Song laughed again, empty and almost unhinged. Go Se-won fell silent.

[P80]
Song wasn’t talking only about the kidnapping.

[P81]
*What is it?*

[P82]
His heart pounded. A current ran down his spine.

[P83]
It was a warning, telling him he should not hear any more. But he found himself asking anyway.

[P84]
“What limit are you talking about, Director?”

[P85]
“A monster who’s forgotten even the most basic duty.”

[P86]
“What?”

[P87]
*Step.*

[P88]
Song stopped before the Teleportation magic circle leading outside. He stared at it for a moment before speaking again.

[P89]
“The boundary between human and monster. That bastard Go Jun…… has already become a monster.”

[P90]
The old man’s empty gaze drifted through the air. As though searching through memories of a brilliant past, he took a weary step toward the magic circle and left Go Se-won with one last plea.

[P91]
“I apologize for what I did to you. So please, don’t let those children die for nothing.”

[P92]
*Flash!*

[P93]
Before Go Se-won could ask another question, the Teleportation magic activated. Dazzling light swallowed Song Cheonwoo.

[P94]
Go Se-won stood alone, staring in confusion at the spot where Song had been. Then he turned.

[P95]
The hallway was made entirely of white marble. At the far end of its long stretch stood a closed door. Behind it, someone was probably sipping wine, pleased with himself.

[P96]
*What in the world…… have you done?*

[P97]
The question rose from somewhere deep inside him.

[P98]
Section A had always been bright. Today, it felt like a pit full of darkness.

[P99]
* * *

[P100]
I had no idea how long I’d been shut away in the training ground—or training room, as they called it in the modern world.

[P101]
One day. Two. Maybe three.

[P102]
The walls blocked out everything beyond them, and the temperature stayed the same. Once I got absorbed in martial arts, I lost track of time.

[P103]
I had a smartphone, but I never checked it. Maybe the people at the Peace Guild had some idea what I was doing, because no one came looking for me or got in touch.

[P104]
“…….”

[P105]
Saying it like that made me sound like a complete loner. Which I absolutely wasn’t.

[P106]
……Probably.

[P107]
*The Skeleton King hasn’t come by once since then, either.*

[P108]
It was good news in one sense: he seemed to be handling things better than I’d expected. But it also meant the emergency rescue team was busier, and more Gates were showing signs of abnormal activity. I couldn’t exactly celebrate.

[P109]
What I *could* celebrate was that my own attempt was nearly complete.

[P110]
*It’s not finished yet, though.*

[P111]
I’d never tried anything like this before, and getting this far hadn’t been easy. The pressure to make something exceptional while the situation outside was ready to explode probably hadn’t helped.

[P112]
*What I have now might be good enough……*

[P113]
Should I just go with it?

[P114]
I’d asked myself that dozens, maybe hundreds of times. I was going over it again when the training room door opened with a familiar mechanical sound.

[P115]
“So this is where you were. I need your help, as it happens.”

[P116]
*Step. Step.*

[P117]
Combat boots polished to a shine. A skin-tight blue suit. A shield with a skull on it.

[P118]
I gave him a look colder than the snow piled on the roof of King Sejong Station in Antarctica.

[P119]
“Look at this fucking bastard.”

[P120]
“You heard from Director King Fury, didn’t you?”

[P121]
“……Are you playing two roles now?”

[P122]
“Heh heh. Surely a citizen of the United States of America ought to be King-tin America.”

[P123]
“This bastard keeps changing his name whenever he feels like it. Want me to beat you so hard you’ll wish you were back on the glacier?”

[P124]
“I can do this all day.”

[P125]
*Whoosh! Boom!*

[P126]
White Flame shot toward him like a streak of light. Its spearhead grazed his neck and pierced the training room wall, burying the shaft.

[P127]
The Skeleton King looked from the spear to me, then muttered, “All day might be difficult……”

[P128]
“Cut the bullshit. Why are you here? If you dropped by because you were bored, I’ll kill you. Seriously.”

[P129]
He answered in a hurry.

[P130]
“N-no, that’s not it. It’s a mission. A mission!”

[P131]
“A mission?”

[P132]
“That is correct, wicked human.”

[P133]
He nodded.

[P134]
“It isn’t an ordinary Mutated Gate. The magical power reading is enormous.”

[P135]
“……!”

[P136]
Damn it.

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;

Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
